partners.diseaseBName: microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type II
partners.mechanism_chain: NPHP4 (HGNC:16975) —DISRUPTS→ Cilium assembly and function (GO:0097059); Cilium assembly and function (GO:0097059) —LEADS_TO→ Renal abnormalities (HP:0000077); PCNT (HGNC:8708) —DISRUPTS→ Centrosome function and duplication (GO:0005813); Centrosome function and duplication (GO:0005813) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); Centrosome function and duplication (GO:0005813) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002650). Loss-of-function mutations in NPHP4 disrupt cilium assembly and function, leading to renal abnormalities characteristic of Senior-Loken syndrome 4. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in PCNT disrupt centrosome function and duplication, resulting in microcephaly and skeletal dysplasia seen in microcephalic osteodysplastic primordial dwarfism type II. While NPHP4's primary role is in cilia, and PCNT's in centrosomes, both structures are intimately linked and essential for cell division, polarity, and development. Defects in either can impinge on shared downstream cellular processes, explaining the overlap in developmental defects.
